metadata.title: EAU Guidelines on Sexual and Reproductive Health
metadata.organization: EAU Guidelines Panel on Sexual and Reproductive Health
metadata.summary: This section addresses the classification and assessment of perceived or anatomical penile shortness, buried penis, and concerns about penile size associated with body dysmorphia. It covers medical and psychosexual evaluation, penile measurements, and non-surgical and surgical approaches to penile lengthening and girth enhancement. It also discusses counselling, treatment complications, and limitations in the evidence.

target_population: Men reporting a short penile size or seeking penile augmentation
Men with adult acquired buried penis
Boys with micropenis or disorders of sex development
Men with congenital or acquired penile shortness
therapeutic_areas: Surgical treatment of adult acquired buried penis

toxicities.event: Postoperative complications after surgery for adult acquired buried penis
toxicities.incidence: The reported incidence reached up to 3.5% for grade V complications.
prevention: Before surgery, encourage lifestyle changes and modification of risk factors, particularly weight loss, to reduce complications and improve outcomes.
Discuss the potential benefits and complications of surgery thoroughly with patients.

toxicities.incidence: The guideline describes a significant incidence but does not provide a rate.
prevention: Discuss possible complications extensively before these procedures.

toxicities.event: Perceived or measured loss of penile length after penile prosthesis implantation
toxicities.incidence: In the study by Deveci et al. involving men undergoing primary implantation because of diabetes or RP, 72% reported a perceived reduction in penile length, although the change in measured SPL was not statistically significant. In a prospective study excluding patients with PD, erect penile length decreased by 0.83 ± 0.25, 0.75 ± 0.20 and 0.74 ± 0.15 cm at 6 weeks, 6 months, and one year after implantation, respectively.
recognition: A patient-reported reduction in penile length may occur without a statistically significant change in measured SPL.

toxicities.event: Arterial thrombosis or loss of reconstructed phallic tissue
toxicities.incidence: In the series by Garaffa et al. of 16 patients, one patient lost the distal third of the reconstructed phallus after acute thrombosis of the arterial anastomosis immediately after surgery. In the series by Falcone et al. of 10 patients, two patients developed acute thrombosis at the microsurgical arterial anastomosis.
recognition: Acute thrombosis at the arterial anastomosis after reconstruction.

management.severity: Acute arterial thrombosis in the series by Falcone et al.
management.actions: Emergency surgical exploration successfully treated the affected patients.

toxicities.event: Neourethral stricture or fistula after reconstruction
toxicities.incidence: In the series by Lumen et al., two patients developed urinary complications comprising stricture and/or fistula. In the series by Falcone et al. of 10 patients, one patient developed a neourethral stricture and fistula.
recognition: Urethral stricture or fistula; in the series by Garaffa et al., these occurred at the anastomosis between the native urethra and neourethra.

management.severity: Urethral stricture or fistula in the series by Garaffa et al.
management.actions: Revision surgery successfully treated these complications.

management.severity: Neourethral stricture and fistula in the series by Falcone et al.

toxicities.event: Penile implant removal or revision after total phallic reconstruction
toxicities.incidence: In the series by Lumen et al., four patients underwent penile implant surgery, and 50% of those implants were subsequently removed. In the series by Falcone et al., three implant recipients required revision surgery: 2 because of infection and 1 because of mechanical failure.
recognition: Implant infection or mechanical failure was reported as a reason for revision in the series by Falcone et al.

management.severity: Implant infection or mechanical failure in the series by Falcone et al.

toxicities.event: Local swelling and inflammatory reaction after penile filler injection
Temporary local pain or swelling after penile filler injection
recognition: Temporary pain or swelling at the treated site.

toxicities.event: Sclerosing lipogranuloma and inflammatory complications after foreign-body injection
recognition: Chronic granulomatous foreign-body inflammation may produce penile sclerosing lipogranuloma, termed paraffinoma or siliconoma according to the injected substance.
Manifestations range from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene.

management.actions: Penile reconstructive surgery may be necessary.

prevention: Do not use silicone, paraffin or petroleum jelly (Vaseline) for penile girth enhancement.

toxicities.event: Graft fibrosis and associated reduction in penile length
associated_therapies: porcine dermal acellular matrix graft (InteXen; American Medical Systems, Minnetonka, MN, USA)
toxicities.incidence: Graft fibrosis was observed in up to 13% of patients. Among patients with fibrosis, the reported mean reduction in penile length was 0.5 cm.
recognition: Graft fibrosis accompanied by loss of penile length.
prevention: Do not use grafts for penile girth enhancement because the procedures are considered experimental.

toxicities.event: Oedema, painful erection or curvature after dermal fat grafting
toxicities.incidence: Penile oedema was reported in up to 27%, painful erection in up to 27%, and curvature attributed to graft fibrosis in up to 9%.
recognition: Penile curvature associated with graft fibrosis.
prevention: Do not use grafts for penile girth enhancement because the procedures are considered experimental.

toxicities.event: Complications or removal of a subcutaneous penile implant
toxicities.incidence: Published data report complications, usually mild and transient, in <5% and an implant removal rate of 1%.
prevention: Do not use the subcutaneous penile implant (Penuma®) for girth enhancement because it is considered experimental.

toxicities.event: Adverse psychological outcomes after penile augmentation
recognition: Some psychologically vulnerable patients do not achieve satisfactory emotional adjustment after augmentation.

Men seeking augmentation who have marked psychological vulnerability, including BDD, may be at risk of worsening psychopathology and suicide attempts and are unlikely to have their surgical expectations met.

management.severity: Psychological vulnerability associated with an augmentation request
management.actions: Provide clinical and psychological support, with an assessment tailored to the patient and consideration of cultural expectations.

prevention: Assess psychological vulnerability and patient expectations before augmentation.
Refer patients with suspected BDD for mental health counselling.

prophylaxis.recommendation: Initiate lifestyle changes and address risk factors, particularly through weight loss, to minimise complications of adult acquired buried penis surgery and optimise its outcomes.
prophylaxis.target_population: Patients being considered for adult acquired buried penis surgery.

infection_management.prevention: Do not use silicone, paraffin or petroleum jelly (Vaseline) for penile girth enhancement; injections of these substances can cause inflammatory complications extending to Fournier’s gangrene.

infection_management.pathogen_or_syndrome: Penile implant infection after total phallic reconstruction
infection_management.management: In the series by Falcone et al., revision surgery was performed in 2 patients because of infection after penile prosthesis implantation.

therapies_index.name: Psychotherapy
approved_indications: Consider when psychopathological comorbidities are identified or aversive relationship dynamics may contribute to a request for penile augmentation.

therapies_index.name: Cognitive behaviour therapy
approved_indications: The guideline states that it could be applied to anxiety about penile size in men with BDD, while noting that no clinical trials have been reported.

therapies_index.name: penile traction therapy
approved_indications: Consider as a conservative means of increasing penile length.
It has also been proven effective for restoring length or correcting deformities due to PD or post-RP conditions.
therapies_index.administration: Study protocols included at least 4 hours/day for 6 months and 4–6 hours per day during the first 2 weeks followed by 9 hours per day until the end of the third month.
key_toxicities: The guideline describes minimal side effects without specifying them.

therapies_index.name: AndroPenis
approved_indications: Used for penile traction therapy in a study of penile dimensions.
therapies_index.administration: 4-6 hours per day for 6 months in the study by Nowroozi et al.

therapies_index.name: Golden Erect
approved_indications: Used for penile traction therapy in studies of penile dimensions.
therapies_index.administration: The study by Nikoobakht et al. used it for 4–6 hours per day during the first 2 weeks and then 9 hours per day until the end of the third month; the study by Gontero et al. used it for at least 4 h/day for 6 months.

therapies_index.name: vacuum erection devices
approved_indications: Generally considered for patients who do not respond to oral ED therapies.
The guideline includes a Weak recommendation to consider them for penile lengthening, although its evidence summary describes them as ineffective for that purpose.
Benefits following PPI and RP are reported.
therapies_index.administration: In a study of penile elongation, a device was used three times a week for 20 minutes on each occasion, for 6 months.

therapies_index.name: oral ED therapies
approved_indications: Mentioned as treatments for ED that may be tried before vacuum erection devices are considered.

therapies_index.name: Testosterone
approved_indications: Described as a treatment to increase penile length in infant or prepubertal boys with micropenis.

The guideline recommends endocrinological treatment to restore penile size in boys with micropenis or disorders of sex development; it recommends against testosterone therapy for increasing penile size after puberty.

therapies_index.name: T
approved_indications: Topical administration is described for infant or prepubertal boys with micropenis.
therapies_index.administration: Topical; no regimen is specified.

therapies_index.name: DHT
approved_indications: Proposed for boys with micropenis, particularly those responding poorly to T or those with type 2 alpha reductase deficiency.
therapies_index.administration: Topical; no regimen is specified.

therapies_index.name: hCG and FSH
approved_indications: Proposed as a combined treatment in the discussion of micropenis in boys; the guideline notes that direct comparisons between proposed endocrinological treatments are unavailable.

therapies_index.name: hCG
approved_indications: Proposed in combination with FSH in the discussion of micropenis treatment in boys.

therapies_index.name: FSH
approved_indications: Proposed in combination with hCG in the discussion of micropenis treatment in boys.

therapies_index.name: androgen-deprivation therapy
approved_indications: Mentioned as a treatment for prostate cancer.
key_toxicities: Identified among treatments associated with chronic intrinsic penile shortening.

therapies_index.name: radiation therapy
approved_indications: Mentioned among treatments for prostate cancer.
key_toxicities: Identified among treatments associated with chronic intrinsic penile shortening.

therapies_index.name: radical prostatectomy
approved_indications: Mentioned as a treatment for prostate cancer.
key_toxicities: Identified as a common cause of chronic intrinsic penile shortening.

therapies_index.name: radical cystectomy
key_toxicities: Identified as a common cause of chronic intrinsic penile shortening.

therapies_index.name: adult acquired buried penis surgery
approved_indications: Consider to restore genital anatomy in AABP.
therapies_index.administration: The guideline recommends undertaking the operation in high volume centres and initiating lifestyle changes and risk-factor modification, particularly weight loss, beforehand.
key_toxicities: Significant postoperative complications are reported, including up to 3.5% of grade V according to Clavien-Dindo Classification.

therapies_index.name: un-burying of penile shaft
approved_indications: Described as a lower-complexity surgical component for AABP.

therapies_index.name: reconstruction of penile shaft with the use of skin flaps or grafts
approved_indications: Described as a lower-complexity surgical approach for AABP.

therapies_index.name: plastic surgical techniques to reconstruct the scrotum
approved_indications: Described among lower-complexity procedures for AABP.

therapies_index.name: escutcheonectomy
approved_indications: Described as a higher-complexity option for AABP involving removal of the suprapubic fat pad.

therapies_index.name: apronectomy
approved_indications: Described as a higher-complexity option for AABP involving the abdominal wall skin and subcutaneous fat.

therapies_index.name: weight loss
approved_indications: Recommended as part of lifestyle and risk-factor modification before AABP surgery to reduce surgical complications and improve outcomes.

therapies_index.name: suspensory ligament release
therapies_index.mechanism: Releases the ligament attaching the penis to the pubic bone.
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for its use in penile lengthening.
therapies_index.administration: Performed through an infrapubic incision; it may be combined with an elongating V-Y skin plasty.
key_toxicities: The guideline associates this procedure, together with ventral phalloplasty and suprapubic fat-reduction procedures, with a significant incidence of complications without specifying individual events.

therapies_index.name: V-Y infrapubic skin plasty
approved_indications: Described as part of a penile elongation and enlargement technique combined with penile lipofilling and SLR.

therapies_index.name: ventral phalloplasty/scrotoplasty
therapies_index.mechanism: Moves the peno-scrotal angle proximally by reshaping ventral shaft skin, increasing exposure of the penile shaft.
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for ventral phalloplasty to address penile lengthening.
therapies_index.administration: The described approach used a longitudinal incision or Z-plasty at the penoscrotal junction and secured the tunica albuginea to the proximal tunica dartos.
key_toxicities: The guideline associates ventral phalloplasty, together with suspensory ligament release and suprapubic fat-reduction procedures, with a significant incidence of complications without specifying individual events.

therapies_index.name: suprapubic lipoplasty/liposuction/lipectomy
therapies_index.mechanism: Reduces suprapubic fat-pad thickness to expose more of the penile shaft.
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for these approaches to address penile lengthening.
therapies_index.administration: Fat-pad reduction may be performed by liposuction or by surgical lipectomy.
key_toxicities: The guideline associates these approaches, together with suspensory ligament release and ventral phalloplasty, with a significant incidence of complications without specifying individual events.

therapies_index.name: Shaeer’s monsplasty technique
approved_indications: Investigated as an approach to increase visible penile length.

therapies_index.name: total phallic reconstruction
therapies_index.mechanism: Creates a new phallus with a neo-urethra.
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for restoring genital anatomy in congenital micropenis.
The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for restoring genital anatomy in genetic males with penile inadequacy caused by traumatic loss.
The procedure is described as reserved for severe penile insufficiency, including congenital micropenis and exstrophy-epispadias complex.
therapies_index.administration: Described approaches include radial forearm free flap, anterolateral thigh flap and musculocutaneous latissimus dorsi (MLD).
key_toxicities: Postoperative complications are reported at a high incidence.
Reported complications in cited series include arterial thrombosis, urethral stricture and fistula.

therapies_index.name: radial forearm free flap
approved_indications: Described as an approach to total phallic reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: anterolateral thigh flap
approved_indications: Described as an approach to phallic reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: musculocutaneous latissimus dorsi (MLD)
approved_indications: Described as an approach to TPR.

therapies_index.name: penile prosthesis implantation (PPI)
approved_indications: Described as implant surgery in men with ED and in reconstructive series.
The guideline recommends against offering it to patients seeking penile lengthening.
key_toxicities: In the study by Deveci et al., 72% of patients perceived a decrease in penile length, although measured SPL did not differ significantly.
In a cited series following traumatic penile loss and reconstruction, implant revision was required in 2 patients because of infection and 1 because of mechanical failure.

therapies_index.name: Alpha-1
approved_indications: Described as a three-piece implant used in a study of primary implant surgery due to diabetes or RP.

therapies_index.name: Ambicor
approved_indications: Described as a two-piece implant used in a study of primary implant surgery due to diabetes or RP.

therapies_index.name: AMS 700 LGX
approved_indications: Used in a study of patients with PD and no deformity or penile curvature < 30° or severe penile fibrosis/scarring.

therapies_index.name: penile disassembly
therapies_index.mechanism: Separates the penis into anatomical components and places autologous cartilage between the glans cap and the ends of the corpora cavernosa.
approved_indications: Studied for penile lengthening, but the guideline recommends against offering it to patients seeking lengthening options.
therapies_index.administration: A cited series used autologous rib cartilage implantation followed by VED therapy.
key_toxicities: Glans necrosis is identified as a possible serious complication.

therapies_index.name: sliding technique (ST)
approved_indications: Described for length restoration with concomitant PPI in end-stage PD with severe shaft shortening; the guideline recommends against offering the sliding technique to patients seeking penile lengthening options.
therapies_index.administration: Described with concomitant PPI.

therapies_index.name: modified sliding technique (MoST)
approved_indications: Described as a modification of ST used in a series involving penile shortening and narrowing due to PD and other aetiologies.

therapies_index.name: multiple slit technique (MuST)
approved_indications: Described as a modification of ST used in a series involving penile shortening and narrowing due to PD and other aetiologies.

therapies_index.name: Hyaluronic acid
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for its use as an injectable material for penile girth enhancement.
The guideline gives a Strong recommendation against its use for girth enhancement in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.
therapies_index.administration: Injection of gel for penile girth enhancement; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Infrequent, mild, temporary side effects are described without further specification.

therapies_index.name: polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA)
approved_indications: Described as an injectable filler used for penile girth enhancement.
therapies_index.administration: Microsphere injection; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Postoperative swelling and inflammatory reactions resolved within a few days in the cited studies.

therapies_index.name: Poly-l-lactic acid (PLA)
therapies_index.mechanism: Stimulates fibroblast proliferation and increases collagen deposition in tissue.
approved_indications: Described as an injectable soft tissue filler used for penile girth enhancement.
therapies_index.administration: Injection; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Temporary local pain and swelling were reported in treated patients.

therapies_index.name: hydroxyethyl methacrylate
approved_indications: Listed as an injectable material used for penile girth enhancement.
therapies_index.administration: Injection; no dose or schedule is specified.

therapies_index.name: polyalkylamide hydrogel (PAAG)
approved_indications: Listed as an injectable material used for penile girth enhancement.
therapies_index.administration: Injection; no dose or schedule is specified.

therapies_index.name: calcium hydroxyapatite
approved_indications: Listed as an injectable material used for penile girth enhancement.
therapies_index.administration: Injection; no dose or schedule is specified.

therapies_index.name: collagen
approved_indications: Identified as a biological filler of human or animal origin.

therapies_index.name: silicone
approved_indications: Described as a substance injected for penile girth enhancement, a use that the guideline strongly recommends against.
therapies_index.administration: Injection is described; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Chronic granulomatous foreign-body inflammation, including siliconoma.
Reported inflammatory complications range from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene.

therapies_index.name: paraffin
approved_indications: Described as a substance injected for penile girth enhancement, a use that the guideline strongly recommends against.
therapies_index.administration: Injection is described; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Chronic granulomatous foreign-body inflammation, including paraffinoma.
Reported inflammatory complications range from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene.

therapies_index.name: petroleum jelly (Vaseline)
approved_indications: Described as a substance injected for penile girth enhancement, a use that the guideline strongly recommends against.
therapies_index.administration: Injection is described; no dose or schedule is specified.
key_toxicities: Chronic granulomatous foreign-body inflammation.
Reported inflammatory complications range from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene.

therapies_index.name: autologous fat injection
therapies_index.mechanism: Transfers fat harvested from the patient into the penile shaft to increase its circumference.
approved_indications: The guideline gives a Weak recommendation for its use in penile girth enhancement.
The guideline gives a Strong recommendation against its use for girth enhancement in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.
therapies_index.administration: Fat is harvested by liposuction, generally from the lower abdomen, and injected into the penile shaft.
key_toxicities: The cited retrospective studies reported no serious adverse events such as penile abscess or deformity requiring reoperation.

therapies_index.name: penile lipofilling
approved_indications: Described in a cited technique combining enlargement and elongation with V-Y infrapubic skin plasty and SLR.

therapies_index.name: grafting procedures (albugineal and peri-cavernosal)
approved_indications: Investigated for penile girth enhancement; the guideline considers graft use for this purpose experimental and gives a Strong recommendation against it.
key_toxicities: The guideline associates grafting procedures with a high complication rate and low patient satisfaction.

therapies_index.name: porcine dermal acellular matrix graft (InteXen; American Medical Systems, Minnetonka, MN, USA)
approved_indications: Studied for penile girth enhancement; the guideline considers girth-enhancement grafting experimental and recommends against it.
therapies_index.administration: A cited study performed the procedure through an infrapubic incision.
key_toxicities: Graft fibrosis was observed in up to 13% of patients in a cited study; patients with fibrosis had a mean penile-length reduction of 0.5 cm.

therapies_index.name: venous grafts
approved_indications: Described for penile girth enhancement; the guideline considers girth-enhancement grafting experimental and recommends against it.

therapies_index.name: dermal fat grafts
approved_indications: Studied for penile girth enhancement; the guideline considers girth-enhancement grafting experimental and recommends against it.
therapies_index.administration: Free grafts consist of deepithelialized dermis and subcutaneous fat; an area of approximately 10 x 5 cm is needed for harvesting.
key_toxicities: Penile oedema up to 27%, painful erection up to 27%, and curvature due to graft fibrosis up to 9% were reported.
Penile hypoesthesia, skin necrosis and infection were not reported in the cited studies.

therapies_index.name: biodegradable scaffolds
approved_indications: Investigated for penile girth enhancement; the guideline considers this use experimental and gives a Strong recommendation against it.
therapies_index.administration: Fibroblasts harvested from the patient's scrotal skin and dartos tissue are cultured, seeded into microporous biodegradable poly-lacti-co-glycolic acid (PLGA) scaffolds, and implanted between Dartos and Buck’s fascia.

therapies_index.name: Penuma®
approved_indications: Described as an approved subcutaneous implant for penile girth enhancement; nevertheless, the guideline considers its use for this purpose experimental and gives a Strong recommendation against it.
therapies_index.administration: A soft silicone implant is placed over 3/4 of the penile shaft and secured to the glans with a polyester mesh.
key_toxicities: Published data cited by the guideline report complications, usually mild and transient, in <5% and implant removal in 1%.

therapies_index.name: revision surgery
approved_indications: Described as treatment for urethral stricture or fistula after total phallic reconstruction.

therapies_index.name: penile reconstructive surgeries
approved_indications: May be required when siliconoma or paraffinoma needs excision.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men requesting penile augmentation who have psychopathological comorbidities or whose request may be influenced by aversive relationship dynamics.
decision_rules: Consider psychotherapy when psychopathological comorbidities are identified or aversive relationship dynamics may contribute to the request for augmentation.
If BDD is suspected, refer the patient for mental health counselling rather than treating psychological vulnerability as an indication for augmentation.

recommended_regimens.name: Psychotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider therapy that addresses the motivations and expectations of the patient and partner and places genital size and shape variation in context. Psychotherapy is not intended to prevent a legitimate choice to seek improvement.

alternative_regimens.name: Cognitive behaviour therapy
alternative_regimens.summary: The guideline states that this approach for BDD could also be applied to anxiety about penile size, but reports no clinical trials for that use.

supportive_care: Arrange evaluation by an accredited mental health expert when BDD/PDD or other psychopathology is suspected.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Some psychologically vulnerable men do not attain satisfactory emotional adjustment after augmentation and may experience adverse effects from invasive procedures.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with excessive concern about a normal-sized penis.
decision_rules: Distinguish anxiety about a normal-sized penis from true micropenis and assess for possible BDD before considering an augmentation procedure.

recommended_regimens.name: Psychotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider psychotherapy when psychopathological comorbidities or aversive relationship dynamics are present; counselling can address expectations about penile size.

alternative_regimens.name: Cognitive behaviour therapy
alternative_regimens.summary: This therapy could be applied to penile-size anxiety, although the guideline reports no clinical trials in this setting.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: Men with SPA may be at risk for BDD.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men seeking a conservative increase in penile length.
decision_rules: Consider penile traction therapy as a non-surgical lengthening option.
The recommendation table also says to consider vacuum erection devises, although its evidence summary describes them as ineffective for lengthening.

recommended_regimens.name: Penile traction therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider traction to increase penile length. The reported effect concerns flaccid and stretched length, not girth; the evidence is limited by small, heterogeneous cohorts and a lack of RCTs.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the Gontero et al. pilot phase-II prospective study, flaccid and stretched length gains were +2.3 and +1.7 cm, respectively (both p < 0.001), without a significant girth change. In the Nikoobakht et al. prospective study, mean flaccid length changed from 8.8 ± 1.2 cm to 10.5 ± 1.2 cm (P < 0.05), and stretched length from 11.5 ± 1.0 cm to 13.2 ± 1.4 cm (p < 0.05) after 3 months. At 6-month follow-up, reported mean gains from baseline in flaccid, stretched and erect length were +1.7 ± 0.8, +1.3 ± 0.4, and +1.2 ± 0.4 cm, respectively (p < 0.001, for all).
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: In the cited Gontero et al. study, at least 4 hours/day for 6 months; the cited Nikoobakht et al. study assessed use over 3 months.

recommended_regimens.name: Vacuum erection devises
recommended_regimens.summary: The recommendation table says to consider these devices for lengthening, despite the evidence summary calling them ineffective for that purpose.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In a study of 27 men with SPL < 10 cm, use three times a week for 20 minutes per occasion over 6 months did not significantly increase flaccid or stretched length.
recommended_regimens.duration_cycles: In the cited study, three times a week for 20 minutes per occasion for 6 months.

response_assessment.method: Measure penile length in the flaccid, stretched or erect state as applicable.
response_assessment.interpretation: The cited traction studies assessed changes in length; the cited vacuum-device study found no significant increase in flaccid or stretched length.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline's recommendation to consider vacuum erection devises conflicts with its evidence summary and cited lengthening study, which describe no demonstrated lengthening benefit.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Infant or prepubertal boys with micropenis, including boys with disorders of sex development.
decision_rules: Use endocrinological treatment to restore penile size in eligible boys.
The guideline reports no direct comparisons among the hormonal approaches it discusses.

recommended_regimens.name: Testosterone therapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Hormonal therapy used to increase or restore penile size before puberty.

recommended_regimens.name: transdermal dihydrotestosterone
recommended_regimens.summary: An endocrinological option for restoring penile size in boys; the guideline reports better outcomes with DHT particularly in poor responders to T or those with type 2 alpha reductase deficiency.

recommended_regimens.name: recombinant gonadotropins
recommended_regimens.summary: An endocrinological approach to restoring penile size in boys. The guideline also describes proposed combined hCG and FSH treatment with positive outcomes.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline does not establish a preferred hormonal approach through direct comparative studies.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men after puberty, including men with late-onset hypogonadism, seeking an increase in penile size.
decision_rules: Do not use hormonal treatment for penile-size enlargement after puberty.

not_recommended.name: testosterone therapy
not_recommended.reason: The guideline states that it does not increase penile size in adult men or men with late-onset hypogonadism; the recommendation against its use after puberty is Strong.

not_recommended.name: other hormonal therapies
not_recommended.reason: The guideline gives a Strong recommendation against their use to increase penile size after puberty.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Adults with AABP being considered for surgical restoration of genital anatomy.
decision_rules: Classify the clinical presentation and surgical requirements, counsel extensively about benefits and complications, and initiate lifestyle and risk-factor changes, particularly weight loss, before intervention.
Consider surgery to expose the penile shaft and reconstruct genital covering; additional removal of suprapubic or abdominal tissue depends on the presentation.

recommended_regimens.name: Lifestyle changes and modification of risk factors
recommended_regimens.summary: Initiate risk reduction, particularly weight loss, to limit surgical complications and improve outcomes.

recommended_regimens.name: surgical treatment
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider an operation to uncover the shaft, reconstruct genital tissues and, when needed, remove surrounding excess tissue. Procedures described range from skin flaps or grafts and scrotal reconstruction to escutcheonectomy or apronectomy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: The guideline reports satisfactory functional outcomes and a low incidence of recurrence, alongside postoperative complications of up to 3.5% of grade V according to Clavien-Dindo Classification.

response_assessment.method: Assess genital function, recurrence and postoperative complications.
response_assessment.interpretation: Satisfactory function and infrequent recurrence are reported, but postoperative complications remain an important risk.

supportive_care: Provide extensive preoperative counselling about expected benefits and complications.
Encourage weight loss and modification of other risk factors before surgery.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation table specifies Strong for performing AABP surgery in high volume centres.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients considered for surgical penile lengthening for congenital intrinsic shortness.
decision_rules: Consider the less complex lengthening procedures according to the anatomy and the surgical objective.
Discuss procedure-related complications extensively and undertake complex penile-shortness surgery in high volume centres.

recommended_regimens.name: Suspensory ligament release
recommended_regimens.summary: A lengthening operation that releases the penile attachment to the pubic bone; an infrapubic approach may be combined with V-Y skin plasty.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the Littara et al. series, which combined penile lipofilling, V-Y infrapubic skin plasty and SLR, resting length increased from 8.8 cm to 11.4 cm, SPL from 12.4 cm to 13.5 cm, resting circumference from 8.3 cm to 11.06 cm, and IIEF-5 from 21.5 to 23 at 12 months.

recommended_regimens.name: ventral phalloplasty
recommended_regimens.summary: Ventral skin reconstruction moves the penoscrotal angle proximally to expose more of the shaft; the section also describes scrotoplasty.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the Xu et al. series of 41 patients, correction succeeded in all patients and median flaccid length improved by +2.1 cm.

recommended_regimens.name: suprapubic lipoplasty/liposuction/lipectomy
recommended_regimens.summary: Reducing the suprapubic fat pad increases visible shaft exposure.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In Ghanem et al., 3 (30%) patients were very satisfied, 5 (50%) satisfied, 1 (10%) neither satisfied nor dissatisfied, and 1 (10%) dissatisfied after liposuction. In the Shaeer’s monsplasty study, visible flaccid length at 3 months was 7.1 ± 2.1cm, a 57.9% improvement, and visible erect length was 11.8 ± 2.1cm, a 32% improvement; satisfaction rate improved by 73.1% at final follow-up (18 months).

response_assessment.method: The cited combined SLR procedure assessed resting length, SPL, resting circumference and IIEF-5.
response_assessment.interpretation: The reported changes apply to the combined procedure, not SLR alone.

supportive_care: Counsel extensively about complications associated with the lengthening procedures.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline associates these procedures with a significant incidence of complications. Its evidence summary says penile-shortness surgery should be reserved for high volume centres, while the corresponding explicit centre recommendation names AABP surgery.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Patients with severe congenital penile insufficiency, including congenital micropenis or exstrophy-epispadias complex, being considered for extensive reconstruction.
decision_rules: Consider total phallic reconstruction to restore anatomy in congenital micropenis when the anticipated benefit warrants its complexity and potential complications.

recommended_regimens.name: total phallic reconstruction
recommended_regimens.summary: A complex reconstructive operation intended to create a new phallus and neo-urethra for severe penile insufficiency.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In Lumen et al., satisfaction was high in 6 cases and moderate in 1; 4 patients underwent penile implant surgery, and 50% of those implants were subsequently removed. In Garaffa et al., almost all patients (93%) were fully satisfied with cosmesis and size; sexual intercourse was achieved in 11 of the 12 patients who underwent PPI.

response_assessment.method: Assess appearance, size, urinary function, sexual function and reconstructive complications.
response_assessment.interpretation: The cited series report satisfactory outcomes but also urethral complications, flap-related complications or subsequent implant removal.

supportive_care: Discuss potential complications when weighing reconstruction against expected benefit.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The recommendation table grades use of total phallic reconstruction for congenital micropenis as Weak; Figure 9.1 labels the reconstructive branch Strong.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with acquired penile shortness seeking a procedure specifically to increase penile length.
decision_rules: Do not offer penile prosthesis implantation, penile disassembly or sliding technique as penile-lengthening options.

not_recommended.name: Penile prosthesis implantation
not_recommended.reason: The guideline finds it ineffective for increasing penile length and gives a Strong recommendation against offering it as a lengthening option.

not_recommended.name: Penile disassembly
not_recommended.reason: Evidence is limited, and significant complications including glans necrosis can occur; the recommendation against offering it for lengthening is Strong.

not_recommended.name: sliding technique
not_recommended.reason: The evidence is limited; the guideline gives a Strong recommendation against offering it to patients seeking lengthening.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline describes reported length gains with penile disassembly and lengthening corporal manoeuvres in selected studies, but does not recommend these techniques to patients seeking lengthening options.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Genetic males with penile inadequacy due to traumatic loss.
decision_rules: Use total phallic reconstruction to restore genital anatomy after traumatic penile loss.

recommended_regimens.name: total phallic reconstruction
recommended_regimens.summary: Reconstruct a phallus after traumatic loss; the cited series used RAFFF, with urethral reconstruction adapted to the remaining anatomy.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: In the Falcone et al. series of 10 patients, all patients with complete urethral repair could void and ejaculate through the phallus. After a median follow-up of 51 months, all were satisfied with size, cosmesis and sensation. 6 patients received a PPI and could engage in penetrative intercourse; 3 patients required revision surgery (2 for infection and 1 for mechanical failure).

response_assessment.timepoint: After reconstruction; median follow-up of 51 months in the cited series
response_assessment.method: Assess voiding, ejaculation, size, appearance, sensation and complications.
response_assessment.interpretation: The cited series reported satisfaction and restored function alongside arterial, urethral and implant-related complications.

treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The evidence summary describes satisfactory outcomes despite a high incidence of postoperative complications.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men seeking an increase in penile circumference who do not have penile dysmorphic disorder.
decision_rules: Counsel extensively about the potential benefits and risks of girth-enhancement techniques.
The guideline weakly recommends hyaluronic acid, soft tissue fillers and autologous fat injection, while strongly advising against the specified foreign-body materials and experimental procedures.

recommended_regimens.name: hyaluronic acid
recommended_regimens.summary: An injectable filler used to enlarge penile girth.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Cited studies report a girth increase of 1.4 to 3.78 cm and patient satisfaction of 78-100%; they report no severe side effects.

recommended_regimens.name: soft tissue fillers
recommended_regimens.summary: The recommendation encompasses soft tissue fillers; the guideline discusses PMMA and PLA as well as HA.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Two cited PMMA studies reported an average circumference increase of 3.5 cm. Cited PLA reports describe an average girth increase of 1.2 to 2.4 cm. The evidence summary describes satisfaction with soft tissue fillers, especially HA, PMMA and PLA, as > 78%.

recommended_regimens.name: autologous fat injection
recommended_regimens.summary: Fat harvested by liposuction is injected into the penile shaft. The guideline notes insufficient long-term data.
recommended_regimens.key_outcomes: Retrospective studies report an average circumference increase of 2 to 3.5 cm and postoperative satisfaction in more than 75% of patients.

not_recommended.name: silicone
not_recommended.reason: Foreign-body injections can cause chronic granulomatous inflammation and complications ranging from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene; the recommendation against use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: paraffin
not_recommended.reason: Foreign-body injections can cause chronic granulomatous inflammation and complications ranging from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene; the recommendation against use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: petroleum jelly (Vaseline)
not_recommended.reason: Foreign-body injections can cause chronic granulomatous inflammation and complications ranging from oedema and infection to Fournier’s gangrene; the recommendation against use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: grafts
not_recommended.reason: The guideline considers girth-enhancement grafting experimental, cites insufficient long-term data and reports a high complication rate and low patient satisfaction; the recommendation against use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: biodegradable scaffolds
not_recommended.reason: The guideline considers this approach experimental because long-term data are insufficient; the recommendation against use is Strong.

not_recommended.name: subcutaneous penile implant (Penuma®)
not_recommended.reason: The guideline considers this approach experimental because long-term data are insufficient; the recommendation against use is Strong.

response_assessment.method: Assess penile circumference, satisfaction and complications.
response_assessment.interpretation: The reported gains and adverse events differ by technique; long-term evidence is insufficient for several approaches.

supportive_care: Provide extensive counselling about the risks and benefits of girth enhancement.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline states that precise indications for girth enlargement are not established. Although it reports promising findings for Penuma®, its formal recommendation is not to use the implant for this purpose.

treatment_pathways.patient_population: Men with penile dysmorphic disorder seeking penile girth enhancement.
decision_rules: Do not use the specified injectable or fat-based girth-enhancement procedures in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.
Address the psychological condition and seek mental health counselling when BDD/PDD is suspected.

recommended_regimens.name: Psychotherapy
recommended_regimens.summary: Consider psychotherapy when psychopathological comorbidity is present, with attention to augmentation expectations.

not_recommended.reason: The guideline gives a Strong recommendation against its use for girth enhancement in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.

not_recommended.reason: The guideline gives a Strong recommendation against its use for girth enhancement in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.

supportive_care: Refer patients with suspected BDD for mental health counselling.
treatment_pathways.special_considerations: The guideline cautions that psychologically vulnerable augmentation candidates may not achieve the expected benefit from an invasive procedure.

conditions.name: short penis condition
conditions.description: A complaint of insufficient penile size that requires distinguishing anatomical shortening, reduced visibility of a normally sized penis, and concern about normal penile dimensions. The document states that no consensus definition of standard penile size exists.
conditions.epidemiology: Perceived penile size adversely affects sexual life in about 10% of men; this proportion is higher among men seeking penile augmentation.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Men may report dissatisfaction with penile dimensions, sexual difficulties or distress about appearance.

subtypes.name: False penile shortness
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Less of a normally sized penile shaft is visible, as occurs with adult acquired buried penis.

subtypes.name: Intrinsic penile shortness
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Penile size is reduced because of congenital incomplete genital development or an acquired process shortening the corpora cavernosa.

subtypes.name: small penis anxiety (SPA)
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Excessive concern about a penis of normal size, distinct from true micropenis.

diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Relevant history includes phimosis, priapism, hypospadias/epispadias, penile trauma, penile cancer, prostate cancer, and penile pain with or without acquired curvature suggestive of PD.

Measurement methods elsewhere in the document include STT and BTT; STT underestimates erect length by about 20%, whereas BTT correlates better with erect length, especially in overweight and obese men.

conditions.name: adult acquired buried penis (AABP)
conditions.description: An acquired condition in which a penis of normal size becomes concealed by prepubic, scrotal or penile tissue or skin, reducing visible and functional length. Chronic inflammation, scarring and progressive entrapment of the shaft may reinforce one another.
conditions.epidemiology: Its exact prevalence is unknown. Incidence appears to be rising alongside obesity, the principal risk factor. Aggressive circumcision, surgical treatment in patients with obesity or penile cancer, and lichen sclerosis (LS) are also described as contributing factors.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Common associated problems include erectile and voiding dysfunction, difficulty maintaining genital hygiene and reduced QoL.

subtypes.name: concealed penis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A term historically applied to congenital buried penis in children.

subtypes.name: webbed penis
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A term historically applied to congenital buried penis in children; abnormal dartos fascia development may entrap the shaft in surrounding tissue.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Determine whether the penile shaft is concealed despite normal penile size.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: Particularly in men with BMI > 30, lichen sclerosis or a history of penile cancer who report urinary or sexual difficulties or poor cosmetic appearance.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Concealment by surrounding tissue supports buried penis rather than intrinsic penile shortness.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document penile dimensions and anatomy for assessment and treatment planning.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During evaluation of the condition.

definitions.description: Procedures may involve exposing the concealed shaft, reconstructing shaft skin with flaps or grafts, or reconstructing the scrotum.
Procedures may include escutcheonectomy or apronectomy.

staging.additional_rules: Available classifications use both clinical presentation and the operation needed; the document does not give numerical stage criteria.

conditions.name: congenital intrinsic penile shortness
conditions.description: Congenital reduction in penile size resulting from incomplete genital development; the category includes true micropenis. Hormonal-axis disturbances associated with genetic syndromes are among the described causes.
conditions.epidemiology: The document reports a prevalence between 0.9% and 2.1% for male genital malformations. Micropenis may occur as an isolated finding without a definitive etiological cause in up to 25% of cases.
conditions.clinical_presentation: A genuinely small penis is present rather than reduced exposure of a penis of normal size.

subtypes.name: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Listed causes include genetic diseases and iatrogenic or traumatic injury to the pituitary gland or hypothalamus.

subtypes.name: Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Listed causes include chromosomal alterations such as Klinefelter Syndrome, Androgen Synthesis Defects and dysgenetic gonads.

subtypes.name: Syndromic or Multiple Congenital Anomalies
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Listed associated conditions are bladder exstrophy–epispadias complex and hypospadias.

diagnostic_workup.test: Genital physical examination and stretched penile length (SPL)
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish whether penile dimensions meet the criterion for micropenis and distinguish intrinsic shortness from concealment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When congenital short penile size is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Micropenis is defined by SPL less than 2.5 standard deviations (SD) below the mean for age and race.

conditions.name: true micropenis
conditions.description: A congenital anatomical condition involving penile length below the age- and race-referenced threshold that results from an underlying genetic or endocrine condition.
conditions.epidemiology: Epidemiological studies report micropenis in between 0.015% - 0.66% of male newborns. The document states that overall incidence in the male population is not clearly documented.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Penile length is genuinely reduced, in contrast to concern about a normally sized penis or concealment of a normally sized shaft.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify anatomical micropenis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When true micropenis is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: SPL is the distance between the pubic symphysis and the glans apex; a value less than 2.5 standard deviations (SD) below the mean for the male's age and race meets the stated criterion.

conditions.name: bladder exstrophy–epispadias complex (BEEC)
conditions.description: A spectrum of congenital genitourinary malformations associated with genital abnormalities, particularly micropenis.
conditions.epidemiology: The stated prevalence at birth is 1/10,000.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Manifestations range from epispadias to bladder exstrophy or exstrophy of the cloaca. Long-term psychosocial and psychosexual difficulties are frequent, and male infertility is often associated with impaired sperm quantity or quality and hormonal impairment.

subtypes.name: epispadias
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Included in the described spectrum of malformations.

subtypes.name: bladder exstrophy
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Included in the described spectrum of malformations.

subtypes.name: exstrophy of the cloaca
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Included in the described spectrum of malformations.

long_term_effects: Psychosocial and psychosexual dysfunction may persist in the long term after surgical reconstruction.

conditions.name: Intrinsic penile shortness – acquired
conditions.description: Actual shortening of the corpora cavernosa following an acquired pathological process. The process may be acute after trauma or amputation, or chronic with progressive fibrosis.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Reduced penile length may follow penile trauma, surgical amputation, PD, treatment for prostate cancer, radical cystectomy, radiation therapy, low flow priapism or multiple penile operations.

subtypes.name: acute
subtypes.distinguishing_features: The document identifies penile trauma and surgical amputation due to penile cancer as common acute causes.

subtypes.name: chronic
subtypes.distinguishing_features: Progressive corporal fibrosis may underlie shortening; frequently identified causes include PD, treatments for prostate cancer and radical cystectomy.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Identify acquired causes and prior genital or pelvic treatment.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When acquired shortening is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Relevant events include trauma, penile or prostate cancer treatment, radical cystectomy and previous penile procedures.

diagnostic_workup.test: Genital physical examination and penile measurements
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Document the degree and form of penile shortening.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment and before treatment planning.

conditions.name: Body dysmorphic disorder (BDD)
conditions.description: A clinical diagnosis involving marked distress about a perceived appearance defect that others do not see or see only slightly, with substantial impairment in important areas of life. The document places it in the Obsessive Compulsive and Related Disorders section of APA's DSM-5.
conditions.epidemiology: Reported prevalence is 2.2% of men in the USA and 1.8% in Germany. BDD is expected in between 3%-16% of patients undergoing cosmetic surgery; the rates stated for men and women are 15.3% and 10.9%, respectively.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Concern about appearance may be accompanied by impaired social or occupational functioning. Among men seeking penile augmentation, psychological vulnerability may place them at risk of worsening psychopathology and suicide attempts; they are unlikely to meet their surgical expectations.

subtypes.name: Muscle dysmorphia
subtypes.distinguishing_features: A form of BDD, usually described in men, involving pronounced concern about perceived insufficient muscularity and body shape; penile size or shape may also become a focus.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Screen for possible body dysmorphic psychopathology.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When BDD is suspected, including in patients with a normal-sized penis who report shortness.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Screening does not replace evaluation by an accredited mental health expert.

diagnostic_workup.test: The Cosmetic Procedure Screening Scale for Penile Dysmorphic Disorder
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Screen for body- or penis-focused dysmorphic psychopathology.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During assessment of psychological risk before a cosmetic penile procedure.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: Screening does not replace evaluation by an accredited mental health expert.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment by an accredited mental health expert
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate BDD/PDD, other psychopathological comorbidities and differential diagnoses.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When BDD is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The document identifies personality disorders and disorders in the obsessivecompulsive, psychotic or emotional spectrum as considerations for differential diagnosis; Gender Dysphoria and Koro must also be distinguished.

conditions.name: Penile Dysmorphic Disorder (PDD)
conditions.description: A shorthand term for BDD in which a perceived deficiency in the size or shape of a normally sized penis is the principal concern. It is not separately listed in APA's DSM-5 coding system and differs from small penis anxiety.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Penile-focused appearance concerns cause mental health impairment and substantial disruption of important areas of life. The condition may become apparent among patients requesting cosmetic procedures.

diagnostic_workup.test: Genital physical examination and penile measurements
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish penile dimensions and distinguish a normally sized penis from true micropenis.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When penile dysmorphia is suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: The described PDD concept concerns a perceived flaw in a penis of normal size or shape.

diagnostic_workup.test: The Cosmetic Procedure Screening Scale for Penile Dysmorphic Disorder
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Screen for penile-focused dysmorphic psychopathology.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During psychological assessment, particularly before a requested augmentation procedure.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An accredited mental health expert is needed for diagnostic evaluation.

diagnostic_workup.purpose: Screen for BDD-related psychopathology.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When dysmorphic concerns are suspected.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: An accredited mental health expert is needed for diagnostic evaluation.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment by an accredited mental health expert
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Evaluate PDD and other psychopathological conditions.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When PDD is suspected.

conditions.name: small penis anxiety (SPA)
conditions.description: Excessive anxiety about a penis that is normal in size. The document distinguishes it from BDD/PDD and true micropenis; SPA is not included in APA's nomenclature.
conditions.clinical_presentation: Concern about penile size despite normal anatomical measurements. Men with SPA may be at risk for BDD.

diagnostic_workup.test: Genital physical examination and penile measurements
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Establish whether penile size is normal.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: When a patient expresses anxiety about a short penis.
diagnostic_workup.interpretation: SPA concerns a penis of normal size rather than true micropenis.

diagnostic_workup.test: Assessment of subjective penile size perception
diagnostic_workup.purpose: Characterise the patient's perception of penile size.
diagnostic_workup.when_indicated: During psychological evaluation.

special_populations.population: Infant or prepubertal boys with micropenis or disorders of sex development
special_populations.considerations: Hormonal treatment may restore penile size in boys with these conditions. Direct comparisons between the proposed treatments are unavailable.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Use endocrinological therapies to restore penile size. The document identifies Testosterone therapy, transdermal dihydrotestosterone and recombinant gonadotropins; DHT has been reported to have better outcomes particularly in poor responders to T or those with type 2 alpha reductase deficiency. Combined hCG and FSH treatment has also been proposed.

special_populations.considerations: Testosterone therapy does not increase penile size in adult men or men with late-onset hypogonadism.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Do not use testosterone therapy or other hormonal therapies to increase penile size after puberty.

special_populations.population: Men with obesity and adult acquired buried penis
special_populations.considerations: Obesity is the principal risk factor for adult acquired buried penis. Surgery can improve function but carries a significant risk of postoperative complications.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Initiate lifestyle changes and risk-factor modification, particularly weight loss, before surgery to reduce complications and optimise outcomes.

special_populations.population: Men with suspected body dysmorphic disorder or penile dysmorphic disorder seeking penile augmentation
special_populations.considerations: Some men seeking augmentation have psychological vulnerability and may be unlikely to achieve their expectations from surgery. An accredited mental health expert should assess suspected psychopathology.
special_populations.treatment_modifications: Refer patients with suspected BDD for mental health counselling. Do not use hyaluronic acid, soft tissue fillers or autologous fat injection for penile girth enhancement in men with penile dysmorphic disorder.

recommendations.statement: Conduct a thorough genital examination to rule out adult acquired buried penis (AABP) in all men, with particular attention to those with BMI > 30, lichen sclerosis or a history of penile cancer who report urinary or sexual difficulties or dissatisfaction with appearance.
recommendations.rationale: Obesity, lichen sclerosis and treatment for penile cancer are identified as risk factors for AABP.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.1.4 Summary of evidence and recommendations for classification

recommendations.statement: Apply classification systems to describe the clinical presentation of AABP and guide its surgical management.
recommendations.rationale: Available systems classify AABP by clinical findings and the surgery required.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.1.4 Summary of evidence and recommendations for classification

recommendations.statement: Ask about body dysmorphic disorder/penile dysmorphic disorder when a patient with a normal-sized penis reports that it is too short.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.1.4 Summary of evidence and recommendations for classification

recommendations.statement: Obtain a comprehensive medical and sexual history from every patient concerned about short penile size.
recommendations.rationale: Both histories are essential to evaluating a complaint of short penile size.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Define penile length using stretched measurements from either the penopubic skin junction or the pubic bone to the glans tip.
recommendations.rationale: The skin junction-to-glans tip measurement may underestimate erect length; the pubic bone-to-glans tip measurement correlates better with erect length, particularly in men with overweight or obesity.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Measure penile length in both flaccid and erect states for a detailed assessment.
recommendations.rationale: These measurements may provide additional information about penile size.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Measure penile girth in every patient who complains of short penile size.
recommendations.rationale: Girth measurements may provide further information about penile size and shape.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Use validated questionnaires to screen for body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) when penile size is normal.
recommendations.rationale: Self-report instruments can help identify patients at risk of psychopathology.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Use validated questionnaires, such as IIEF-15 and BAPS, to establish baseline sexual function and beliefs about penile size.
recommendations.rationale: Validated instruments can assist with assessing sexual function and size-related beliefs.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Refer patients in whom BDD is suspected for mental health counselling.
recommendations.rationale: Mental health counselling helps identify psychological vulnerability among men requesting penile augmentation.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.2 Diagnosis

recommendations.statement: Consider psychotherapy when psychopathological comorbidities are identified or adverse relationship dynamics may be motivating a request for penile augmentation.
recommendations.source_heading: 9.3.1.5 Summary of evidence and recommendations for the non-surgical management of short penile size

recommendations.statement: Consider penile traction therapy as a conservative option for increasing penile length.
recommendations.rationale: Penile traction therapy has increased length in the flaccid and stretched states, although the supporting evidence is of poor quality.
